detailed_rationale:
Jubilant FoodWorks is the master franchisee for Domino's Pizza in India (2,513 stores as of Jun-2026) plus Popeyes India, international Domino's (Sri Lanka/Bangladesh/Nepal) and Turkey via DP Eurasia. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 14.1% YoY to Rs 2,569.3cr, but this was driven by network expansion (net 76 stores added group-wide, 58 by Domino's India) rather than existing-store demand: Domino's India like-for-like (LFL) growth was just 2.5% -- continuing a clear deceleration from 9.1% in Q2 FY26 (delivery-led, +16.5% YoY) to 5% in Q3 FY26. FY26 full-year LFL was 6.5% (vs 7.5% in FY25, ~7% two-year average), and management's own comment that 'Q1 FY27 LFL will be higher than Q4 FY26' implies Q4 FY26 was the weakest print of the year. Growth is increasingly a unit-expansion story (~300 stores/yr targeted for FY27) layered on decelerating, mid-single-digit same-store volumes -- the volume-vs-price/network-led growth distinction that should discount the headline revenue number.

On earnings quality: FY26 consolidated PAT from continuing operations was Rs 386cr (+54.4% YoY) on Rs 9,512.5cr revenue (~4.1% PAT margin); Q4 FY26 continuing-ops PAT was ~Rs 80cr (+66-67% YoY) with EBITDA margin at 19.4% (+69bps) and PAT margin 3.7% (+107bps). The large % PAT growth is flattered by a genuinely small base and by FY26's reclassification of the loss-making Dunkin' India franchise (Rs 372cr revenue, Rs 191cr net loss, franchise non-renewed through Dec-2026) plus the Russian subsidiary (Pizza Restaurants LLC) divestment as discontinued operations. This is a legitimate portfolio cleanup, not a red flag, but it does mean YoY continuing-ops comparisons sit against a lighter, restated base -- checked and cleared as a genuine one-off, not an earnings-quality inflation. Turkey (DP Eurasia) is now a real contributor: continuing-ops PAT +150% YoY, margin +274bps to 7.5%. Into FY27, management has explicitly flagged fresh margin headwinds -- labour code rollout (~20bps) and minimum-wage hikes across 11 states (~20-30bps) plus commodity inflation -- being offset by only a ~1.2% cumulative price hike, premiumization and cost control, so further margin expansion is not a given.

On valuation: at ~Rs 28,949cr market cap and a trailing PE near 65x (scorecard pe_current 65.2, value_score only 24.3/100), the multiple prices a QSR compounder well beyond what the disclosed growth algorithm (5-7% guided LFL + ~8-9% unit growth = mid-teens topline, margin expansion now contested) can deliver for long. ROE 16.4% / ROCE 23.4% are respectable, not exceptional, for the multiple paid; D/E ~2.1x is a lease-driven (Ind AS 116) retail-network artifact, not balance-sheet distress. Price action already reflects the deceleration: 12-month return -37.5%, 6-month return -19.9%, both 50/200-DMA broken -- the stock has been de-rating, but from a starting multiple still rich enough that a further re-rate toward mid-teens realistic growth is plausible.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score (final_score_3y 38.8, final_score_1y 37.3, recommendation_overall Sell) already flags this on rich valuation (value_score 24.3) despite decent quality (quality_score 77.2). My own research agrees rather than creates tension: same-store growth is decelerating (9.1% to 5% to ~2.5% over three straight quarters), the headline revenue growth is now mostly store-count-driven, and FY27 carries fresh, company-acknowledged wage/commodity margin headwinds only partly offset by a 1.2% price hike. This is not a coin-flip case for rescue -- I am not overriding the quant Sell.
summary: Jubilant FoodWorks' (Domino's India franchisee) revenue growth is now being carried mostly by new-store openings rather than existing-store demand -- same-store sales growth has decelerated from 9.1% to 5% to just 2.5% over the last three quarters, below management's own 5-7% target band for the coming year. FY27 also brings fresh wage and commodity cost pressure that the company is only partly offsetting with a small price hike. At roughly 65 times trailing earnings, the stock is priced for a stronger growth and margin story than the company itself is currently guiding to, so we recommend continuing to Sell / stay out despite the underlying business (store network, brand, returns on capital) being fundamentally sound.
positive_para: Domino's India remains a structurally scaled, franchise-protected network (2,513 stores, clear #1 in organized pizza) with real unit-economics visibility -- ~300 stores/yr guided -- and growing multi-geography optionality: Turkey (DP Eurasia) has turned into a genuine profit contributor, continuing-ops PAT +150% YoY with margin expanding to 7.5%. The FY26 portfolio cleanup (exiting loss-making Dunkin' India and the Russian subsidiary) is rational capital discipline that should lift consolidated margins going forward even absent any demand improvement. ROE 16.4% / ROCE 23.4% show real returns on deployed capital, and management is not silent on cost risk -- it has already quantified the FY27 wage-inflation hit and moved on pricing/premiumization to defend margin.
negative_para: The core worry is that revenue growth is increasingly a store-count/unit-expansion story rather than a demand story: Domino's India LFL growth nearly halved from 9.1% (Q2 FY26) to 5% (Q3 FY26), and Q1 FY27 printed just 2.5% -- below the low end of management's own 5-7% FY27 guidance band and a continuation, not a reversal, of the deceleration. On top of a softening topline, FY27 brings fresh, company-acknowledged margin headwinds (labour code + 11-state minimum-wage hikes, ~40-50bps combined, plus commodity inflation) met with only a modest 1.2% cumulative price increase -- the operating-leverage story investors are paying 65x trailing earnings for is not obviously intact. Should LFL stay sub-5% for another 1-2 quarters while cost headwinds bite, the multiple has real further downside; the stock's 12-month return of -37.5% shows the market has already started pricing this in without yet reaching a level consistent with mid-teens realistic growth.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~65x trailing PE, the market is pricing a growth/margin trajectory well ahead of disclosed guidance: 5-7% LFL + ~8-9% net store growth implies mid-teens topline, and FY27 margin is more likely flat-to-slightly-up (wage/commodity headwinds roughly offsetting the 1.2% price hike and premiumization) than materially expanding. A reverse-DCF at this multiple effectively needs high-teens-to-20%+ earnings compounding sustained for a decade -- not supported by the observed deceleration (LFL nearly halving Q2-to-Q3 FY26, and just 2.5% in Q1 FY27). Verdict: RICH -- a price-paid problem, not a business-quality problem.
